mechanism_narrative: When the monthly FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the S&P 500 returns positively despite the policy signal.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 50,000 jobs predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the employment increase (p > 0.05), or the effect is not significant in a multiple regression controlling for inflation and GDP proxies.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds the prior quarter's value by at least 2%, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting excess demand for equities.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after the consumption signal (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is reversed in a regression with supply proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 5% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals corporate risk aversion.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the production decline (p < 0.05), or the effect is not robust to controls for interest rates and inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and optimism.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the effect disappears when controlling for FEDFUNDS movements.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both PAYEMS (jobs) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 10,000 and 5% respectively over the next month indicate a labor-driven economic expansion that boosts equity valuations.
regime_hint: dual labor and retail demand expansion
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically positive after the interaction signal (p > 0.05), or the interaction term is insignificant in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained 3-month decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) below 3%, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to deflationary expectations dampening equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite the CPI decline (p < 0.05), or the effect is absent in a regression with forward yield and earnings momentum controls.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) falls by more than 10% in the next month relative to the prior month, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to housing market weakness and reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are unexpectedly positive after the housing signal (p > 0.05), or the effect is not significant in a multiple regression with macroeconomic controls.
